name: mafioso-menace
style: 1997 New York mafioso rap, dark and cinematic but bare, 90 BPM. A heavyset Brooklyn kingpin reads his rulebook: very deep plummy chest voice, wheezy and humid, slight rasp, audible slow breaths between lines, unhurried and lazily behind the beat, sentences landing anywhere in the bar, calm total authority, never shouting, faint bemused smirk. Gritty East Coast boom bap: laid-back heavily swung drums pitched down, booming dusty kick, crunchy cracking snare, tight hi-hat, short ominous minor-key jazz piano stab looped like a held breath, low upright bass hum, vinyl crackle, warm tape saturation, mono-ish mid-90s mix with the voice dry and loud up front. Between rules a turntable scratch cuts a gruff shouted announcer voice counting the number. No hook, no chorus, no singing.
exclude: trap, 808 rolls, rattling hi-hats, autotune, melodic singing, sung chorus, choir, modern polish, EDM, synth pads, high-pitched voice, shouting rap, fast double-time flow
lyrics:
[Intro: deep calm spoken, slow breath]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Scratch: shouted count "One!"]
[Verse: relaxed, behind the beat]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Scratch: shouted count "Two!"]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Scratch: shouted count "Three!"]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro: low, slow, spoken, beat drops out]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]
